plainTranslation: Person A (Mercury)'s reasoning and expression can meet a forceful challenge from the Person B (Mars) person. Person B (Mars) may hear a question as opposition to an intention; Person A (Mercury) may hear an assertive reply as criticism of an idea. Person A (Mercury) can answer more insistently or become occupied with defending the argument, which Person B (Mars) may experience as further provocation. The square describes difficulty coordinating expression with assertion, not proof that one person is irrational or deliberately hostile. Mental stimulation is possible, but repeated exchanges can become more concerned with defeating the other person's point than understanding it. The contact alone does not establish who dominates or how either person normally handles disagreement.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.

summaryDeep: Their questions, explanations, and way of talking press against your drive, timing, and willingness to act. It catches often enough that you both feel it, and it keeps asking to be worked out. Name it directly instead of letting it build in silence.
tension: The invitation of this aspect is deeper self-understanding. It shows you where your nervous system speeds up before your mind has a chance to catch up. It reveals the stories you tell yourself about being misunderstood, criticized, or unheard. And it asks both people to become more conscious of how they speak, listen, and respond.
advice: The growth here comes from not reacting to every disagreement. This person will get under your skin sometimes. You will probably do the same to them. If both of you can stay in the conversation instead of immediately defending yourselves, you can learn a lot from the differences between you. Workable if both slow the reflex to snap; debate the idea, not the person.
summaryShort: Their questions, explanations, and way of talking press against your drive, timing, and willingness to act.
